paper.name: Illustrative paper: gaps already closed in-text
paper.one_line: The authors evaluate clear weather, rain, fog, and night, compare two strong baselines, and state no further open questions beyond routine scaling.

established.research_question: Does the detector remain accurate across weather and lighting when trained with a multi-condition dataset?
established.methodology: Multi-condition training and evaluation; mAP reported per weather bucket; comparison to two published baselines.
findings: mAP stays within a small band across clear, rain, fog, and night splits.
Outperforms both baselines on the authors' multi-condition benchmark.
limitations: Compute cost is higher than a clear-weather-only model (acknowledged, measured).
Closed-loop driving still out of scope — same as many perception papers.
conclusions: Within the multi-condition camera benchmark, the method is presented as evaluated end-to-end for the stated question.
Authors do not list adverse weather as future work; they treat it as addressed.

gap_assessment.summary: No clear research gap is supported beyond routine extensions. The paper already evaluates the obvious robustness conditions. This tool will not invent a gap.
gap_assessment.invented_gap_warning: Do not manufacture a weather-robustness gap — the paper already reports those experiments.

author_future_work.text: Scale training to a larger multi-city corpus when available.
author_future_work.practical_meaning: A scaling / data-volume direction, not an untested scientific limitation.

next_steps.title: Follow the authors' stated scaling direction
involves: Train on a larger multi-city set if you have access.
Keep the same per-condition mAP protocol.
next_steps.would_help_establish: Whether accuracy holds as data scale grows — matching stated future work.

next_steps.title: Compare against a newer baseline (not a paper-supported gap)
involves: Evaluate both on the same multi-condition splits.
next_steps.would_help_establish: Relative standing vs newer methods — this is an extension, not evidence of a gap left open by the paper.
next_steps.literature_note: Choosing which baseline is 'newer' requires literature outside this paper.

suggestions: Replicate on a newer public benchmark the authors did not use.
Investigate only an explicitly stated future direction — do not invent a gap.

from_uploaded_paper: Adverse conditions are already evaluated in the paper's own tables.
Future work is limited to scaling data, not new untested phenomena.
would_need_related_literature: Whether a newer architecture would beat this result.
Whether multi-city scaling is still an open contribution in the field.

adjacency.topic_anchor: Multi-condition camera object detection for driving
adjacency.stay_close_rule: Stay on multi-condition driving perception. Prefer scaling and comparison extensions the authors already allow — do not invent a weather gap.
